summary.title: Zettelkasten
summary.one_liner: The Zettelkasten overview site lays out the core principles, note-linking habits, and writing and reading workflows behind the Zettelkasten personal knowledge method, with links to deeper articles.
takeaways: Use atomic notes: one topic per note, each with its own ID, and link notes to each other instead of relying on search alone.
Prefer tags over categories, and avoid the Collector's Fallacy by working with material (taking reading notes and writing Zettel) rather than just bookmarking or highlighting.
Draft writing projects by building an outline and pasting in Zettel notes, separating composing from editing.
Read thoroughly where it matters and skim the rest, using the Barbell Method of Reading; extract specific information while reading.
Luhmann's history and the author's macOS app, The Archive, are covered, with the site noting it no longer reviews paid tools.
summary.summary: This is the overview hub of zettelkasten.de, a site about the Zettelkasten note-taking and knowledge-work method. It groups posts into Knowledge Management, Writing, and Reading sections, and includes a Principles section (atomicity and connectivity), a Common Questions list, and links to an introduction, history of Niklas Luhmann's Zettelkasten, use cases, and tool pages for The Archive macOS app. The content is a set of short guidance points and links to longer posts rather than a single in-depth tutorial.
